page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.16-128 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance built on AMD EPYC 9J45 processors running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The instance provides 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs under an x86_64 microarchitecture, utilizing simultaneous multithreading with two threads per core. With dedicated CPU core allocation, it delivers predictable compute execution across all threads without contention from oversubscribed neighbor environments.

The configuration provides 128.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance includes no integrated local storage and contains no discrete GPU hardware accelerators. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address, while persistent storage must be attached through external block volumes over the network infrastructure.

With its balanced processing-to-memory footprint and absence of attached local drives, VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.16-128 delivers resource-efficient capacity for workloads requiring consistent multi-threaded compute without paying for dedicated storage media. The server is well suited for general enterprise applications, mid-sized relational database engines, microservices clusters, continuous integration workers, and horizontally scaled web serving.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.16-128 is a balanced general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor clocked at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 16 physical cores configured with two threads per core to deliver 32 dedicated vCPUs alongside 128.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a classic 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. It operates without integrated local storage or graphics acceleration hardware, relying on external network-attached volumes for persistent data retention. Network capabilities feature one complimentary public IPv4 address. This resource distribution makes the instance cost-efficient for compute and memory tasks that do not mandate high-speed local disk caches, rendering it suitable for mid-tier database hosting, web application servers, container orchestration, and continuous integration pipelines.
